m4-t1.question: What should remain stable when Jira menu names differ?
options: The exact location of every button
The work hierarchy and workflow meaning
m4-t1.explanation: Learn the control concepts rather than a brittle click sequence.

m4-t1.question: What should a Review-to-Done transition require?
What is an acceptable substitute if Jira is unavailable?
options: A spreadsheet implementing the same records and transitions
Buying a subscription to receive marks
m4-t1.explanation: Tool access is not the learning outcome.

m4-t1.question: Which information must stay out of a public Jira sandbox?
m4-t1.explanation: Public practice systems are not authorised personal-data repositories.

m4-t1.question: What is the purpose of dependency links?
options: Assign every task to the same person
m4-t1.explanation: Links support coordination; they do not perform the work.

m4-t2.question: Why might an overdue filter miss problematic work?
options: Some items have no due date
All missing dates mean tasks are finished
m4-t2.explanation: Missing dates require their own hygiene check.

m4-t2.question: How should a new filter first be tested?
options: By asking the sponsor to guess
Against records with known expected membership
Only by choosing an attractive chart
By assuming no syntax error means correct logic
m4-t2.explanation: Known cases test the meaning as well as syntax.

m4-t2.question: A colleague sees fewer dashboard records. What is one plausible reason?
options: The data must be identical for everyone
m4-t2.explanation: Visibility can vary by permissions and filter sharing.

m4-t2.question: Why are ticket counts a weak individual ranking?
options: Items differ in complexity and value
Every ticket measures exactly one hour
The busiest chart always identifies the best worker
m4-t2.explanation: Use work evidence and context, not simplistic surveillance metrics.

m4-t3.question: What is throughput?
m4-t3.explanation: Throughput measures completions within a stated period.

m4-t3.question: Under stable conditions, what cycle time corresponds to WIP 12 and throughput 4 per week?
Why monitor work-item age?
options: It reveals delay in unfinished work
m4-t3.explanation: Ageing shows current risk before items finish.

m4-t3.question: Review has reached its WIP limit. What is the useful response?
options: Help clear the bottleneck before starting more work
m4-t3.explanation: The limit should trigger collaboration and policy-based action.

m4-t3.question: What must be stated when reporting cycle time?
options: The start and finish boundaries and calendar basis
m4-t3.explanation: Measurements are interpretable only with consistent definitions.

questions.question: A Jira filter shows no overdue items, but four active records lack dates. What should the dashboard say?
options: No dated overdue matches; missing dates need separate review
The four undated items are completed
The query proves full data quality
questions.explanation: Zero matches do not resolve missing-field uncertainty.

questions.question: A board has Review WIP 5 against a limit of 3 while staff start more work. What is the useful intervention?
options: Raise the limit forever without evidence
Help clear review and inspect the bottleneck policy
questions.explanation: WIP limits should trigger collaboration, not cosmetic compliance.

questions.question: Stable average WIP is 15 and throughput is 5 items weekly. What can be inferred under consistent boundaries?
options: Each employee completes three items daily
Lead time must be exactly one week
Average cycle time is about three weeks
Every item is guaranteed in three weeks
questions.explanation: Little’s Law relates averages under stated system assumptions.

questions.question: Two dashboard users see different issue counts from the same saved filter. What should be checked first?
options: Whether Jira changes project scope automatically
questions.explanation: Different visibility can explain different counts.

questions.question: An item has waited twelve days in review while completed-item average cycle time is four days. What should be highlighted?
options: Ageing unfinished work as a current risk
That the item must be finished already
questions.explanation: Completion averages can conceal open-item delays.

questions.question: A team puts student phone numbers in public issue comments to simplify testing. What is the correct response?
options: Copy the numbers into more screenshots
Remove exposure through the authorised process and use synthetic data
Keep it because the board is convenient
questions.explanation: Public practice tools are not authorised personal-data stores.

questions.question: A workflow has a Done column but no exit criteria. What should be established before relying on completion counts?
options: A rule that old cards become Done
Shared acceptance and quality evidence for the transition
questions.explanation: Counts are meaningful only when state semantics are agreed.

questions.question: An automation would close an issue when its due date passes. Why is this a poor completion rule?
options: Time passing does not prove acceptance
questions.explanation: Completion is an evidence state, not a calendar event.

questions.question: A query is syntactically valid but excludes the intended project. What test would catch this?
options: Expected-result checks using known fixture records
Trusting the lack of an error message
questions.explanation: Logic must be tested independently of syntax.

questions.question: Throughput rises after splitting every ticket into tiny fragments. What must interpretation consider?
options: Changed item definitions and whether value flow improved
questions.explanation: Changing units can change counts without changing useful delivery.
